ads_ratio.reason: Pan American is a direct-listed foreign private issuer: one NYSE-traded PAAS share is one common share, so no ADS conversion applies; per-share figures and the traded price are on the same basis.
ads_ratio.source: Form 40-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-18, SEC CIK 771992), cover page: securities registered under Section 12(b) are 'Common Shares, No Par Value', trading symbol PAAS, listed directly on the New York Stock Exchange — the NYSE security is the common share itself, not an ADS

moat_against: Pure commodity price-taker: earnings are set by silver/gold prices it does not control (Q2 2026 realized silver $70.97/oz vs $32.91 a year earlier — the price, not the company, did the work)
Depleting asset base: reserves are consumed by production and must be continually replaced via M&A or exploration success
Jurisdiction risk: Mexico, Peru, Bolivia, Argentina exposure; Escobal (Guatemala) has been suspended since 2017
Growth has been bought, not built: Yamana Gold (2023) and MAG Silver (2025) were paid for largely in shares — diluted share count CAGR +21.9%/yr in the engine blend
Juanicipio is operated by Fresnillo plc (56% JV partner), not by Pan American — no operational control of its best asset
Cyclical, volatile owner's earnings: OE/share spans negative to $2.67 over the last 5 fiscal years
moat_for: Scale: one of the world's leading silver producers, with operating mines across Canada, Mexico, Peru, Bolivia, Argentina, Chile and Brazil
44% of Juanicipio (via MAG Silver, closed Sept 2025): large-scale, high-grade, low-cost silver mine adding near-term cash flow and reserves
Industry-leading silver reserve base, hard to replicate given permitting scarcity for new primary silver mines
Net-cash balance sheet (engine: net debt -$501M, -1.19x normalized OE) funds capex, dividends and buybacks without forced dilution
Diversification across many mines and two metals (silver + gold) cushions single-mine outages
moat_justification: Weak-to-moderate moat: Pan American is one of the world's largest silver producers with a diversified portfolio of operating mines across the Americas, a 44% interest in the high-grade, low-cost Juanicipio mine (added via the MAG Silver acquisition, closed Sept 2025), a large reserve base, and a net-cash balance sheet — scale, diversification and reserve scarcity that smaller miners cannot replicate. But it is fundamentally a commodity price-taker on depleting assets: it has no pricing power over silver or gold, reserves shrink with every ounce produced and must be replaced by acquisition or exploration, several operations sit in higher-risk jurisdictions, and its flagship growth asset is operated by Fresnillo, not by Pan American. That profile scores 4/10 on the sweep rubric (in line with other diversified price-taking miners), giving CAP = 7.2 years.
name: Pan American Silver Corp.
one_liner: Price-taking silver/gold miner, moat 4/10 — does not clear 15% at $43.77: weighted IRR 5.48%, weighted IV@15 $10.10 on normalized OE; the price capitalizes spot metal prices (latest-FY OE $2.67/sh) persisting and growing, and clears 15% only below ~$10.10 on the normalized base.
